chronicle.text: Youmerei tied fiber and fiber together with fiber and was left with something to carry things in: the first carrier.
Touhas came back for food left 4 weeks before, and it was still there.
Dounetho tied wood and wood together with fiber and was left with something that floats and carries someone across water: the first raft.
Zeitouzi gathered food that had grown where seeds had been dropped: the first harvest from seed left in the ground.
Saigel struck flint with flint and stared at what happened.
Saigel struck flint with flint and was left with a sharp edge: the first blade.
Bebovein went back to what they had left in one spot a third time, to see it happen again: the first deliberate testing.
Disos scratched a mark <\/.> into rock.
Dounetho attacked Zeitouzi: the first violence.
Saigel set food aside on purpose, having found it there when it was needed before: the beginning of keeping stores.
Bebovein buried seed on purpose, having seen it come back as food: the beginning of farming.
Keman tied stone and wood together with fiber and was left with something heavy on a handle: the first club.
Keman drank from the sea and it did not quench their thirst.
Youmerei struck flint where dry things lay, and they caught: the first fire made by people.
3 people now tell that Disos stole from Shogal. It was Youmerei. The story changed as it was passed on.
At (21, 38) the heap of things people had left grew big enough to keep out a fifth of the winter cold: the first dwelling. Dounetho had put in the most.
Hadai found that what Saigel had told them was wrong, and trusted them less for it.
Heinoda tied a club and fiber together with fiber and was left with something warm to wear: the first wrap.
Neilaiya tied a club and a blade together with fiber and was left with a sharp point on a long shaft: the first spear.
4 people now take the mark <o/.> to go with shelter, and have for two years. Nobody decided this; it grew from where the mark was made and seen.
A thirsty year: 3 people died for want of water.
